title: 16 g from 20 g theoretical
hook: Compare the product obtained to the theoretical maximum.

knows: Actual and theoretical yields measure the same product.

misconception: Percent yield is actual mass divided by any reactant mass.
objective: Calculate percent yield from actual and theoretical product masses.

claims.text: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 20 g of a product and an actual yield of 16 g of that same product. What is the percent yield? Percent yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100 = 16 ÷ 20 × 100 = 80%.
The bars show the supplied idealized values for the same product; no specific chemical reaction is implied.
Recall: Which ratio gives percent yield when multiplied by 100? Percent yield compares the actual product obtained with the theoretical product yield.
A 100% yield would mean the measured product mass equals the theoretical product mass for this calculation.

recall.question: Which ratio gives percent yield when multiplied by 100?
recall.why: Percent yield compares the actual product obtained with the theoretical product yield.
